samples.summary: The new drag destination bypasses the surface pin: `checkSurfaceScope` never inspects `action.to.reader`
samples.evidence: `const cited = [action?.type === "read" || action?.type === "wait" ? action.reader : null, action?.target?.reader, action?.expect?.read];` — `action.to.reader` is absent from the list. `assertSafeActionPlan` (scripts/agent/hunt-ui-probe.mjs:162-163) only prefix-checks a target reader against ALL surface namespaces (`UI_READER_PREFIXES`), so `{ type: "drag", target: {reader:"slides.elementCenter",args:["card"]}, to: { reader: "sheet.cellCenter", args: ["B2"] } }` passes plan validation AND the surface scope check on a slides run, and an unknown reader such as `to: {reader:"slides.nope"}` likewise escapes the "unknown reader … Available readers:" refusal that every click target gets. The bridge then throws (`requireSheet`: "sheet reader used while surface is …"), so the action fails with an opaque error instead of the designed refusal — and `classifyUiError` (hunt-ui-probe.mjs:241) only recognises `goto the (sheet|doc) surface first`, so the slides variant keys as `other:<message>`, degrading replay fingerprints. Every other reader-bearing field is in `cited`; `to` was simply not added with the action.

samples.summary: Drag on a role target can crash on a null bounding box and ignores the per-action timeout budget
samples.evidence: `await t.locator.boundingBox().then((b) => ({ x: b.x + b.width / 2, ... }))` dereferences `b` unconditionally. Playwright's `Locator.boundingBox()` resolves to `null` for an element that has no box (hidden / zero-size), so the action fails with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'x')` rather than a readable refusal naming the target — and if the role never resolves the call blocks for Playwright's DEFAULT timeout, because unlike the sibling branches (`click`: `timeout: timeoutMs` at line 290; `scroll`: `hover({ timeout: timeoutMs })` at line 320) no timeout is threaded into `boundingBox()`. `observeAction` has no outer race, so the action can outlive the budget it was admitted under.
searchedFor: grep timeoutMs in hunt-ui-runner.mjs — no setDefaultTimeout, no Promise.race around runAction

samples.summary: checkSlidesDrag dereferences unchecked reader results, so one refusal aborts the entire oracle run
samples.evidence: `const after = await one("badge"); const centre = { x: after.x + after.w / 2, ... }` and, in the resize block, `const card = await one("card")` used as `const wantW = 1700 - card.x` plus `const after = await one("card"); ... after.w`. `one()` returns `null` whenever `slides.elements` refuses (which this very surface is documented to do after certain states — see #883 handling at line 601-632) or when the id is missing. A null then throws a TypeError that escapes `checkSlidesDrag`, aborting the whole verify script — exactly the failure the file's own comment at line 570 ("Unguarded, a refusal here made `before.value.x` a TypeError that escaped `checkSlidesTargeting` and aborted the whole oracle run") was written to prevent. Only the first `before` read is guarded.

samples.summary: A drag on a role target skips Playwright actionability (no scroll-into-view / visibility), so the press can land off-viewport and silently do nothing
samples.evidence: `click` uses `target.locator.click(opts)`, which scrolls the element into view and waits for it to be stable before pressing. The drag branch instead reads `boundingBox()` and presses with raw `page.mouse`, so a control that is scrolled out of the 1600x1200 viewport yields coordinates outside it and the press lands on nothing — no error, no refusal. The reader path is protected against exactly this (`sheet.cellCenter` refuses a scrolled-away cell, asserted at verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:1614), so the guard exists for one end of the vocabulary and not for the new one; "it ran and moved nothing" is the failure mode this change says it most wants to avoid.

samples.summary: The documented snap rule is incomplete: resize also snaps sizes to peers (`matchSize`) and moves also get equal-spacing/equal-distance corrections (`smartGuides`)
samples.evidence: The charter states the hazard as "within 8 slide-logical pixels of another element's edge or centre, the slide's centre, or a guide, the dragged element snaps" and then claims resize round trips are exact. In `packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:6437-6439` a resize runs through `matchSize(...)`, which snaps `w`/`h` to ANY non-selected peer's `w`/`h` within 8 units (`packages/slides/src/view/editor/smart-guides.ts:374-402`) — a size hazard, not a position one, and not mentioned anywhere. At editor.ts:5254 a move runs `smartGuides(...)`, which applies a further correction of up to 8 px for equal-spacing / equal-distance configurations (smart-guides.ts:39-355) — neither is an "edge, centre or guide". Conversely `snapDelta` (snap.ts:79-103) has no other-element CENTRE candidate at all, so the documented list is both over- and under-stated. An explorer following this text will predict an exact resize near a peer's size, see it snapped, and report a defect that is not one — the precise false finding the section exists to prevent. The verify script's header comment (verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:660-665) repeats the same incomplete rule.

samples.summary: `uiDefectKey` ignores a drag's destination, so two different drags from the same origin collapse into one defect key
samples.evidence: `const on = target(action)` reads only `action.target` (hunt-ui.mjs:370-377). For the new action the destination is half the gesture: "drag badge to pointAt(700,800)" and "drag badge to pointAt(300,300)" produce the identical key `persona|drag|slides.elementCenter|<reader>|<op>|<ground>`. The comment at 384-395 states that erring toward OVER-splitting is deliberate because "two defects collapsing into one loses a real finding with no record"; adding `to` to the vocabulary without adding it here reintroduces that collapse.

samples.summary: `slides.pointAt`'s off-slide refusal only explains the width, even when it is the y coordinate that is out of range
samples.evidence: `slides.pointAt(${x}, ${y}) is off-slide — a slide is ${handle.slideWidth} wide in these coordinates` is emitted for a y-axis violation too (e.g. `pointAt(100, 5000)`), where the number quoted is irrelevant and the message misdirects the caller. The height is available as the canvas rect's height / the same scale.

verdict.reason: checkSurfaceScope's `cited` list (hunt-ui-tool.mjs:187) contains only the read/wait reader, `target.reader` and `expect.read`; `action.to.reader` is absent, and its own comment (176-179) enumerates only three reader sites. No other layer supplies the missing scope check: the plan validator's drag case (hunt-ui-probe.mjs:154-163) routes `to` through assertTarget→assertReader (77-82), which is a namespace-prefix test against UI_READER_PREFIXES (61) covering ALL surfaces; the zod `to` field (hunt-ui-tool.mjs:565) is an unconstrained string reader; the out-of-process runner re-checks prefixes only (hunt-ui-runner.mjs:146-148) and resolves `action.to` directly (296-298); and the tool's only pin is the single checkSurfaceScope call at 405. The sole backstop is the page bridge throwing at runtime (bridge.ts:171-190), which yields an opaque error instead of the designed "unknown reader … Available readers" refusal, and for slides falls outside classifyUiError's `(sheet|doc)` regex (hunt-ui-probe.mjs:241), keying as `other:<msg>` (243) and degrading replay fingerprints. Tests confirm the gap: hunt-ui-tool.test.mjs:150-184 exercises read/wait/target/expect/goto only, with no drag/`to` case.

verdict.reason: Code is present exactly as described. hunt-ui-runner.mjs:301-305 dereferences the result of `t.locator.boundingBox()` (`b.x`, `b.width`, ...) with no null check, and Playwright returns null for an element with no box. The path is reachable: resolveTarget (209-212) returns kind:"role" for any {role} target and no plan validator restricts drag targets — `assertSafeActionPlan` exists only as a comment at line 268, with no implementation anywhere under packages/frontend/scripts. The timeout claim also checks out: `click` passes `timeout: timeoutMs` (290) and `scroll` passes `hover({timeout: timeoutMs})` (320), but boundingBox() receives no timeout and no page/context setDefaultTimeout is configured anywhere in packages/frontend (openPage, 353-370), so it can block for Playwright's 30s default against a 10s budget (DEFAULT_ACTION_TIMEOUT_MS, line 66). observeAction (381-388) awaits runAction inside a bare try/catch with no outer race, so the action can outlive its budget and the null dereference surfaces as an opaque TypeError string instead of a refusal naming the target. Missing-guard/opaque-error-handling and budget non-enforcement are squarely in the Correctness lane; no refutation ground applies.

verdict.reason: The code is present as described. `one()` at verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:674-677 returns null both when `slides.elements` refuses (`all.ok === false`) and when the id is absent (`find` → undefined). Three dereferences are unguarded: line 701-702 (`after.x + after.w / 2` after `const after = await one("badge")`), line 717+734-742 (`const card = await one("card")` used as `1700 - card.x`, `card.y`, `card.x`, `card.y` — the early-return at 719-722 guards `slides.elementCenter`, a different reader, not `card`), and line 731+736-742 (`after.w`, `after.h`, `after.x`). Only the first read `before` (689-693) is guarded, exactly matching the reviewer's claim. Refusal is a normal outcome of `readReader` (301-305, resolves `{ok:false}` on rejection), and the file documents `slides.elements` refusing in the #883 state (620-646). The escape path is real: `checkSlidesDrag` is awaited bare at line 1617 with no per-check try/catch; the enclosing catch at 1670-1678 rethrows anything that is not a missing-Chromium message, so a TypeError here aborts the run before `checkSlidesTargeting` (1622), `checkSheetToolbar` (1627), `checkUndoCapability` (1642), `checkSeededFault` (1647) and the funnel checks (1659-1669) run. That is a null-deref crash on a documented path, major under the correctness rubric, and precisely the failure the comment at 570-576 exists to prevent.
